title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules
authors: Suri, H.; Keselman, Y.; Legel, L.; Govette, J.; Mullen, B.; Choradia, N.; Sartawi, T.; Abtin, F.; Moghanaki, D.; Thomson, C. C.; Yankelevitz, D. F.; Ahuja, Y.
abstract: BackgroundThe Lung-RADS algorithm standardizes the management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules, but its risk assessment is driven chiefly by nodule size and attenuation. This misallocates a meaningful fraction of patients: a nontrivial share of small malignancies receive 12-month surveillance while large benign nodules proceed to invasive workup. Artificial intelligence (AI) may supply risk information independent of the imaging features Lung-RADS already uses. MethodsWe validated LungAI, an investigational deep learning nodule malignancy classifier not yet cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), on the held-out NLST test partition of Ardila et al. (2,747 low-dose CT examinations from 1,244 patients with [≥]1 solid or part-solid 4-30 mm nodule; 89 pathologically confirmed cancers, prevalence 3.2%). We compared discrimination against Sybil, mean nodule diameter, and estimated nodule volume. A board-certified radiologist assigned Lung-RADS v2022 categories to a positives-enriched random subset (226 eligible examinations; 78 cancers), projected to the full cohort by contingency weighting. A per-category reclassification algorithm shifted patients along the existing Lung-RADS management ladder using a-priori score cutpoints. We evaluated a separately locked follow-up configuration on examinations with a prior scan. ResultsLungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88-0.95) and AUPRC 0.47 (0.35-0.61), outperforming Sybil ({Delta}AUROC 0.07; {Delta}AUPRC 0.18), diameter ({Delta}AUROC 0.14; {Delta}AUPRC 0.34), and volume ({Delta}AUROC 0.14; {Delta}AUPRC 0.38; all P<0.001). Against Lung-RADS v2022 scored ordinally on the weighted annotated subset, LungAI improved AUPRC ({Delta}AUPRC 0.31, P=0.003) but not AUROC ({Delta}AUROC 0.03, P=0.20). LungAI added discriminative information independent of diameter (likelihood-ratio {chi}2=161, P<10-36; {Delta}AUROC 0.10) and, on follow-up examinations, independent of delta diameter, volume doubling time, and new-nodule status ({chi}2=79, P<10-18). Integrated with Lung-RADS, LungAI reduced cancers on the slowest (12-month rescan) pathway by 46% (3.1[->]1.6 per 1,000 examinations) and benign biopsy referrals by 20% (32.7[->]26.2 per 1,000 examinations) at approximately unchanged total biopsy volume (51.0[->]50.1 per 1,000). Assuming full adherence to recommended follow-up, the combined approach yielded 25 months of net diagnostic lead time, an estimated net cost saving of [~]$2,200, and 6.5 fewer benign biopsies per 1,000 examinations; accounting for published adherence rates, it yielded 1.6 additional cancer diagnoses within 1 year per 1,000 examinations. ConclusionsLungAI contributes malignancy-risk information orthogonal to the size- and growth-based features underlying Lung-RADS and improves the allocation of screening patients across the existing management spectrum while potentially decreasing invasive procedures for benign lesions. Multi-site, multi-geography validation is required to demonstrate practical generalizability.

infographic.key_insight: LungAI refined lung nodule risk assessment beyond size-based features and, when integrated with Lung-RADS, reduced cancers assigned to 12-month surveillance by 46% and benign biopsy referrals by 20% in the study analysis.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This imaging AI study—not a cancer drug discovery study—suggests potential to improve screening triage by identifying higher-risk nodules while reducing unnecessary invasive workup.
method: Validated a deep learning malignancy classifier on held-out NLST low-dose CT examinations.
Compared performance with Sybil, nodule diameter, volume, and radiologist-assigned Lung-RADS v2022.
Used prespecified score cutpoints to reclassify cases along existing Lung-RADS management pathways.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 2,747 examinations from 1,244 patients, including 89 cancers, LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 and AUPRC 0.47; versus weighted Lung-RADS assessments, AUPRC improved significantly but AUROC did not.
infographic.watch_item: LungAI is investigational and not FDA-cleared; triage estimates relied on a weighted, cancer-enriched annotated subset rather than prospective clinical implementation.
infographic.paper_title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules

title: Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT): An NCI-CIBMTR genomic medicine initiative in hematopoietic cell transplantation
authors: Gadalla, S. M.; Lee, N.; Wu, X.; Pirsl, F.; Schmidt, G.; Rafati, M.; Hutchinson, A.; Vogt, A.; Hicks, B.; Liu, J.; Wang, J.; Gaddam, S.; Li, S.; Saber, W.; Chanock, S.; Kraft, P.; Savage, S. A.; Hong, H. G.; Spellman, S. R.
abstract: BackgroundGenomic studies in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are limited by sample sizes and targeted approaches. MethodsThe Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT) project is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the CIBMTR(R) designed to investigate recipient and donor determinants of HCT outcomes. We are generating genome-wide SNP-array genotyping for all samples, and sequencing and methylation profiling for selected subsets. We report study design and cohort characteristics and present two proof-of-concept analyses: comparison of conventional and machine learning prediction of overall survival after HCT in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and assessment of inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) among 19,750 HCT donors using polygenic scores (PGS). ResultsGS-BMT includes 30,718 donor-recipient pairs who received allogeneic HCT in the United States between 2000 and 2019. In AML, clinical variables alone provided modest prediction for post-transplant survival, with similar performance for Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models (C-index=0.63, 0.62, and 0.62, respectively). In donors, CHIP-PGS did not differ by age (p=0.76) but was modestly lower in unrelated vs. related donors (-0.06 standard deviation [SD]; p=0.002). In an illustrative analysis assuming risk of event increases by 50% or 80% per PGS-SD, the top 5.2% and 12.3% of the donors, respectively, would have at least twice the risk of a donor with the average PGS. ConclusionsGS-BMT establishes a large genomic platform aiming to improve individualized risk prediction, donor selection, and precision medicine in HCT.

infographic.key_insight: GS-BMT establishes a large donor–recipient genomic research platform for blood and marrow transplantation, rather than an AI drug-discovery study.
infographic.clinical_relevance: The initiative aims to improve transplant risk prediction and donor selection, but the reported analyses do not establish clinical utility.
method: Genome-wide SNP genotyping of 30,718 donor–recipient pairs, with sequencing and methylation profiling in selected subsets.
Compared Cox, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia.
Assessed inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis using polygenic scores in 19,750 donors.
infographic.evidence_signal: Clinical-variable survival models showed similarly modest discrimination (C-index: 0.63, 0.62, 0.62), while donor polygenic scores differed slightly by relatedness but not age.
infographic.watch_item: The polygenic-score risk scenarios were illustrative assumptions, not demonstrated clinical risk estimates, and require outcome validation before informing donor selection.
infographic.paper_title: Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT): An NCI-CIBMTR genomic medicine initiative in hematopoietic cell transplantation

title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
authors: Wood, D. E.; Ballew, B. J.; Roy, J.
abstract: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. Such strategies will likely involve the use of liquid biopsies, which can analyze biomarkers found in blood for the presence of cancer. We introduce Blackjack, a new detection approach that focuses on the fragmentation patterns of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Blackjack characterizes a persons cfDNA fragmentation sites with a position probability matrix (PPM) that encodes information about the sequence context of the sites. For classification, Blackjack computes two features that represent the similarity of an individuals PPM to those of known healthy and cancer cohorts. With these two features, Blackjack then uses logistic regression to classify a new sample as being from a healthy individual or a person with cancer. In cross-validation experiments using two external whole genome sequencing datasets, Blackjack showed high performance, achieving a minimum area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993 and minimum sensitivity (Sn) of 91.8% (at 98% specificity). This high performance was also present for stage I (AUC 0.991, Sn 89.8%) and stage II cancers (AUC 0.993, Sn 90.2%), and across eight different cancers (minimum AUC 0.985, minimum Sn 80.0%). We demonstrate that Blackjacks accuracy is stable at low simulated sequencing depths ([~]0.24x), and that tissue of origin prediction using Blackjacks similarity measures is high (minimum 82% accuracy of the top two predicted tissues). Our findings show that cfDNA fragmentation site contexts have valuable signals for early cancer detection, and that developing diagnostics with machine learning can benefit from a focus on having a small number of informative features.

infographic.key_insight: Blackjack uses just two cfDNA fragmentation-similarity features to detect cancer with high accuracy in cross-validation, including early-stage disease.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This blood-based detection approach could support less invasive multi-cancer screening, but the study concerns cancer detection—not drug discovery—and does not establish clinical screening utility.
method: Encode DNA sequence context around plasma cfDNA fragmentation sites in position probability matrices.
Calculate similarity to reference matrices from healthy and cancer cohorts.
Use the two similarity features in logistic regression to classify samples.
infographic.evidence_signal: Cross-validation on two external whole-genome sequencing datasets yielded minimum AUC 0.993 and sensitivity 91.8% at 98% specificity overall; stage I sensitivity was 89.8% and stage II sensitivity was 90.2%.
infographic.watch_item: Prospective validation in representative screening populations is needed to determine real-world performance and clinical utility.
infographic.paper_title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns

title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
authors: van der Graaf, F.; Antonissen, N.; Scholten, E. T.; Schalkx, H.; Prokop, M.; Jacobs, C.
abstract: ObjectiveTo compare LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports. Materials and MethodsIn this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologists scores were the reference standard. Each LLM was evaluated with four different prompting strategies: two without Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and two with CoT (one zero shot, one few shot). The automated labelling methods were evaluated against the radiologist primarily using Cohens Kappa, and additionally sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores. ResultsGPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement for seven out of nine SIFs: aortic valve disease, bronchiectasis, consolidation, coronary artery calcification, emphysema, abnormality in mediastinal lymph nodes, and thyroid abnormalities, with Cohen {kappa} values of 0.81 (0.70, 0.93), 0.97 (0.93, 1.00), 0.71 (0.62, 0.82), 0.92 (0.87, 0.96), 0.91 (0.84, 0.97), 0.71 (0.62, 0.80), and 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) respectively. For the remaining two SIFs, moderate LLM agreement was obtained with MedGemma-4B-IT and with GPT-4-Turbo with Cohen {kappa} values of 0.48 (0.40, 0.60), 0.42 (0.31, 0.58) for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass respectively. The highest agreement was obtained with the non-CoT prompt strategies for most SIFs. ConclusionThis study demonstrated that LLMs can automatically label radiology reports with agreement ranging from almost perfect to moderate, but not one LLM - prompt combination achieved the highest agreement across all SIFs.

infographic.key_insight: LLMs labeled incidental findings in lung cancer screening CT reports with moderate to almost perfect agreement, but no model–prompt combination performed best across all nine findings.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This report-labeling research could support incidental-finding data extraction in lung cancer screening; it did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Retrospective analysis of 300 CT reports from one Dutch academic hospital.
Compared GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, and keyword search against radiologist labels.
Tested four prompting strategies per LLM, with and without chain-of-thought.
infographic.evidence_signal: GPT-5 achieved Cohen’s κ of 0.71–0.97 for seven findings; the highest reported agreement for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass was moderate (κ=0.48 and 0.42, respectively), and non-chain-of-thought prompts performed best for most findings.
infographic.watch_item: The small, single-center retrospective dataset limits generalizability; broader validation is needed before clinical implementation.
infographic.paper_title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis

title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)
authors: Hum, R. M.; Christofi, M.; Smith, S. L.; Tan, Y.; Shukla, R.; Marshall, L. M.; Smith, M.; Williams, A.; Orozco, G.; Viatte, S.; Buch, M.; Barton, A.; Ho, P.; Martin, P.
abstract: BackgroundSynovial inflammation in psoriatic arthritis (PsA) lacks a validated histological classification framework. Current approaches apply rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovial pathotypes to PsA, which overlooks immunobiological differences between the diseases and limits the predictive power of tissue stratification. We aimed to define data-driven, PsA-specific synovial pathotypes to facilitate tissue-driven precision medicine. MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were obtained from 61 patients with PsA (n=22), seropositive RA (n=23), seronegative RA (n=10), and other inflammatory arthritides (n=6). Sections underwent multi-modal staining, including H&E, picrosirius red, and immunohisto-chemistry for CD3, CD20, CD68, CD138, and CD31. Whole-slide digital image analysis and automated pixel classifiers quantified cellular and stromal metrics. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified intrinsic PsA pathotypes, which were correlated with clinical disease activity, radiographic osteoarthritis (OA), and longitudinal treatment responses. FindingsWhile a subset of PsA patients shared an inflammatory signature with seropositive RA, unsupervised clustering of the PsA cohort revealed three distinct, novel pathotypes: Dense Myeloid (macrophage-driven), Fibro-Stromal (fibrosis and pauci-immune), and Angio-Lymphoid (hypervascular with significant CD138+ plasma cell infiltration). Pathotypes were independent of treatment and concurrent radiographic knee OA. The Fibro-Stromal pathotype correlated with significantly higher cutaneous psoriasis severity. Longitudinally, patients with the Fibro-Stromal pathotype exhibited a trend toward lower treatment response (44%) following standard interventions (methotrexate or TNF inhibitors) compared to the Dense Myeloid (50%) and Angio-Lymphoid (80%) pathotypes. InterpretationWe present the first computationally derived synovial pathotypes specific to PsA, revealing distinct plasma cell and fibrotic architectures not captured by RA-centric models. To enable clinical translation, we distilled these findings into a pragmatic, four-marker diagnostic decision tree (CD31, CD68, CD138, and picrosirius red) designed for routine histopathology workflows, providing a staging ground for biomarker-stratified clinical trials in PsA. FundingFunding from the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre: Manchester, Arthritis UK, the Wellcome Trust, Brit-PACT, the National Psoriasis Foundation, and the Medical Research Council. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSThe potential clinical utility of tissue-based patient stratification is well established in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), where baseline synovial pathotypes (lympho-myeloid, diffuse-myeloid, and pauciimmune) have guided targeted biologic therapy in landmark precision medicine trials. However, psoriatic arthritis (PsA) exhibits a fundamentally distinct synovial microenvironment, characterised by unique vascular architecture, altered stromal fibroblast phenotypes, and distinct immune infiltrates intertwined with the IL-23/IL-17 cytokine axis. Consequently, attempting to classify PsA synovial tissue using established RA-derived scoring systems risks misrepresenting intrinsic disease biology. There is currently no validated, disease-specific histological classification system for PsA, which forces therapeutic decision-making to rely on an empirical, trial-and-error approach rather than underlying target tissue pathobiology. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to define data-driven, computationally derived synovial pathotypes entirely specific to PsA. By leveraging multi-modal digital pathology and unsupervised machine learning, we deconstructed the PsA synovium into three biologically distinct pathotypes: Dense Myeloid, Fibro-Stromal, and Angio-Lymphoid. We demonstrated that the highly inflammatory PsA microenvironment is distinctly driven by CD138+ plasma cells rather than the CD20+ B cells typically observed in RA. Furthermore, we identified a striking tissue-level divergence: patients with the highly fibrotic, pauci-immune Fibro-Stromal pathotype exhibited the most severe cutaneous psoriasis and demonstrated a trend toward higher failure rates on standard therapies, independent of concurrent osteoarthritis. Crucially, we translated these high-dimensional computational findings into a pragmatic, four-marker diagnostic decision tree (incorporating CD31, CD68, CD138, and picrosirius red). Implications of all the available evidenceThis study establishes that PsA synovial pathology requires a dedicated, disease-specific classification framework. The proposed diagnostic decision tree can be integrated into routine clinical histopathology workflows without the immediate need for advanced spatial or single-cell transcriptomics. Furthermore, the correlation between the Fibro-Stromal pathotype, severe skin disease, and poor joint response to standard therapies provides a biological rationale for stratifying this specific subgroup towards early IL-17 or IL-23 inhibitor intervention alongside conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Ultimately, these novel PsA pathotypes provide the vital staging ground required to design and execute biomarker-stratified, tissue-driven clinical trials, paving the way for precision medicine in PsA.

infographic.key_insight: Computational analysis identified three psoriatic arthritis synovial pathotypes—Dense Myeloid, Fibro-Stromal, and Angio-Lymphoid—rather than cancer drug discovery targets.
infographic.clinical_relevance: These tissue patterns may support future treatment stratification in psoriatic arthritis, but are not validated for clinical decision-making.
method: Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies from 61 patients, including 22 with psoriatic arthritis.
Multi-modal staining and automated whole-slide image analysis quantified immune, vascular, and fibrotic features.
Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified pathotypes and explored clinical and treatment-response associations.
infographic.evidence_signal: In the small psoriatic arthritis cohort, reported treatment-response rates were 44% for Fibro-Stromal, 50% for Dense Myeloid, and 80% for Angio-Lymphoid, described as a trend.
infographic.watch_item: The small discovery cohort and lack of reported independent validation limit conclusions about treatment prediction.
infographic.paper_title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)

title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
authors: Shi, R.; Svirsky, S. E.; Balogun, W. G.; Zeng, X.; Fedak, J. D.; Nafash, M.; Brodman, S. T.; Okonkwo, D. O.; Puccio, A. M.; Karikari, T. K.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) are two common forms of neurotrauma that can present with overlapping clinical features, complicating early diagnosis and management particularly in acute and mixed-trauma settings.1-3 Accurate and rapid biological differentiation remains an unmet need.4 We hypothesized that brain-derived tau (BD-tau), an ultrasensitive blood-based biomarker preferentially selective for tau protein originating from the brain, would distinguish TBI from SCI. In a multi-cohort assessment of 342 patients admitted to the neuro-intensive care unit (285 with TBI, 57 with SCI), and 22 controls, baseline serum BD-tau concentrations were markedly elevated in TBI compared with SCI, discriminating between the two populations with high accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]=0.91, 95%CI 0.87-0.96). In paired serum-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples, serum BD-tau significantly outperformed CSF BD-tau for injury-type discrimination (AUC=0.95, 95%CI 0.89-0.99 vs. 0.80, 95%CI 0.71-0.89). Baseline serum BD-tau also showed superior discrimination of TBI from SCI compared with established blood biomarkers of neurotrauma, including neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (AUC=0.82, 95%CI 0.76-0.88; vs. 0.53, 95%CI 0.43-0.63; 0.67, 95%CI 0.58-0.76; 0.71, 95%CI 0.64-0.79; all DeLong p<0.001). Longitudinally, serum BD-tau remained persistently elevated in TBI, but not SCI, for up to 144 hours post-injury, with distinct temporal trajectories between injury types. Together, these findings indicate that serum BD-tau enables rapid and minimally invasive differentiation of TBI from SCI and may support early clinical decision-making, triage, and enrollment into injury-specific therapeutic trials, highlighting the potential of circulating biomarkers to improve precision diagnostics in acute neurotrauma care.

infographic.key_insight: Serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) distinguished traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI), supporting its potential as an injury-specific neurotrauma biomarker.
infographic.clinical_relevance: If validated, blood-based BD-tau testing could support early neurotrauma differentiation, triage, and injury-specific trial enrollment.
method: Measured baseline serum BD-tau in multiple cohorts comprising 285 TBI patients, 57 SCI patients, and 22 controls.
Compared injury-type discrimination with paired cerebrospinal fluid measurements and established blood biomarkers.
Tracked serum BD-tau trajectories up to 144 hours after injury.
infographic.evidence_signal: Serum BD-tau distinguished TBI from SCI with an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.96) overall and outperformed established blood biomarkers in a comparison analysis (AUC 0.82 versus 0.53–0.71; all DeLong p<0.001).
infographic.watch_item: Findings from neuro-intensive care cohorts require validation in broader acute-care populations, including patients with concurrent brain and spinal cord injuries.
infographic.paper_title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses

title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
authors: Tang, S.; Younes, K.; Penukonda, E.; Hausle, I.; Thropp, P.; Lupo, J. M.; Tosun, D.
abstract: Open-source deep learning models promise scalable quantification of MRI-visible perivascular spaces (PVS), an emerging marker of glymphatic dysfunction in Alzheimers disease (AD). Whether these models remain valid when applied to heterogeneous AD cohorts and preserve ground-truth derived biological associations has not been established. We benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models (nnU-Net T1, nnU-Net T1+FLAIR, mcPVS-Net, MedNet-PVS, ADNI-PVS-Net) against manual labels in 60 multi-site ADNI-3 participants balanced across cognitively unimpaired, mild cognitive impairment, and AD dementia, and in 12 publicly available scans from the VAscular Lesions Detection and segmentatiOn challenge (VALDO) challenge. We evaluated overall, voxel, object, and lesion-wise Dice; stratified performance by region, diagnosis, scanner, PVS severity, and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden; and tested whether model-derived PVS burden reproduced ground-truth derived associations with AD-related biomarkers. Despite high internal performance, all models showed a specialist-generalist trade-off: the AD-trained ADNI-PVS-Net achieved highest internal performance (overall Dice = 0.58{+/-}0.14) but degraded most externally (Dice [≤] 0.11), while MedNet-PVS and mcPVS-Net generalized externally (Dice 0.27-0.30) but systematically misestimated PVS burden. Models were relatively robust across scanner and diagnosis but inconsistent across PVS severity, and some misclassified up to 32% of WMH as PVS. Notably, only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS-amyloid biomarker relationship; other models returned a null result, despite comparable or superior Dice scores. These findings show that internal segmentation accuracy and external generalizability alone do not guarantee downstream inferential validity. Careful model selection and cohort-specific validation against manual labels should precede clinical inference in AD.

infographic.key_insight: In this Alzheimer’s MRI study—not cancer drug discovery—strong PVS segmentation accuracy did not guarantee preservation of biologically meaningful associations.
infographic.clinical_relevance: Model choice may alter research conclusions about PVS burden and Alzheimer’s biomarkers, supporting cohort-specific validation before clinical inference.
method: Benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models against manual labels.
Evaluated segmentation across brain regions, diagnoses, scanners, PVS severity, and white matter hyperintensity burden.
Tested whether model-derived PVS burden reproduced manual-label associations with Alzheimer’s biomarkers.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 60 ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans, ADNI-PVS-Net achieved internal Dice of 0.58 ± 0.14 but external Dice ≤0.11; only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS–amyloid relationship.
infographic.watch_item: External validation was limited to 12 scans, and some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as PVS.
infographic.paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease

title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
authors: Sanchez, E.; Connon, P.; Pasternak, M.; Abrahao, A.; Keith, J.; Dilliott, A. A.; Baril, A.-A.; Frank, A.; Lang, A. E.; Pollock, B. G.; Marras, C.; Fischer, C. E.; Seitz, D.; Dowlatshahi, D.; Grimes, D. A.; Tang-Wai, D. F.; Sahlas, D. J.; Rogaeva, E.; Finger, E.; Tan, K.; Binns, M. A.; Tartaglia, M. C.; Borrie, M.; Freedman, M.; Goncalves, R. A.; Swartz, R. H.; Hegele, R. A.; Dixon, R. A.; Mirza, S. S.; Farhan, S. M. K.; Black, S. E.; Kumar, S.; Pasternak, S. H.; Rajji, T. K.; Steeves, T.; Swardfager, W.; Zetterberg, H.; Kvartsberg, H.; Munoz, D. P.; Zinman, L.; Strong, M. J.; Masellis, M.
abstract: Elevated plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species are proposed as specific biomarkers of Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology but have also been reported in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Their profile across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, as well as their discriminatory value when combined with other plasma biomarkers, remain uncertain. We studied 551 participants (ages 40.1 to 87.1 years; 207 women), comprising 506 patients from the Ontario Neurodegenerative Disease Research Initiative (ONDRI) multi-site cohort and 45 amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls from the Brain-Eye Amyloid Memory study. Ten diagnostic groups were studied: mild cognitive impairment (MCI), AD, Parkinsons disease subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU), MCI, and dementia, frontotemporal dementia (FTD), cerebrovascular disease (CVD) subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI), ALS, and the control group. Baseline visit plasma measurements included p-tau217, p-tau181, A{beta}42/40, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Cross-sectional analyses compared biomarker levels as well as p-tau217-based inference of amyloid positivity status across diagnostic groups. Receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) analyses ascertained the discriminatory capacity of these biomarkers and ratio combinations. Within the ALS group, baseline biomarker measures were also tested for association against baseline clinical features as well as longitudinal measures of neuropsychological change. P-tau217, p-tau181, GFAP, and NfL differed across groups (all P < 0.001). Compared to controls, p-tau217 was elevated in AD and ALS, p-tau181 and GFAP only in AD, and NfL in ALS and FTD. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity was more probable in MCI, AD, ALS, and cognitively impaired CVD groups compared to controls (all P < 0.05). The p-tau217 to NfL ratio discriminated ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.97) compared to p-tau217 alone at 0.65 (95% CI 0.52-0.76). No ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived correction for multiple comparisons. Elevated p-tau217 and inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in ALS provide further evidence that the assay signal is not necessarily specific for AD pathology. However, the use of p-tau217 in combination with NfL provides improved discriminatory power between ALS and AD, supporting the use of plasma biomarker combinations rather than sole reliance on individual plasma biomarkers. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in cognitively impaired CVD may indicate AD and/or cerebral amyloid angiopathy co-pathology. Currently available plasma biomarkers should therefore be used as diagnostic complements and interpreted within clinical context rather than as standalone molecular diagnoses.

infographic.key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 was elevated in both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), while the p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD better than p-tau217 alone.
infographic.clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that interpreting p-tau217 alongside NfL may improve research-level differentiation of ALS and AD, but do not establish a clinical diagnostic test.
method: Studied 551 participants across 10 diagnostic groups, including 45 amyloid-PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls.
Measured baseline plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP.
Compared biomarker profiles and ROC-AUC performance; tested clinical and longitudinal associations within ALS.
infographic.evidence_signal: The p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.97), versus 0.65 (95% CI 0.52–0.76) for p-tau217 alone.
infographic.watch_item: Amyloid positivity was inferred from p-tau217 rather than independently confirmed across patient groups, limiting interpretation of elevated p-tau217.
infographic.paper_title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
